content.value: ## भाग 1: अध्याय प्रवेश: परीक्षा दृष्टिकोण एवं विगत प्रश्न

RPSC’s current Paper IV syllabus places phrasal verbs and idioms in application, one-word substitutes, and often-confused or misused words in the 20-mark Grammar & Usage section. The exam tests whether a candidate can select a word that fits a sentence, not merely recite a list. Learn each expression with a short meaning, its grammar pattern, and a natural example.

Phrasal verbs can have more than one meaning. The entries here teach the meaning shown in the example; they are not exhaustive dictionary definitions. In formal reports, prefer a precise verb when an idiom would sound conversational.
## भाग 2: संकल्पना विस्तार: Vocabulary in Sentence Context
### 2.1 Phrasal verbs for common exam contexts

| Phrasal verb | Meaning in this example | Example |
|---|---|---|
| carry out | perform | The team carried out an inspection. |
| look into | investigate | The department will look into the complaint. |
| set up | establish | The district set up a help desk. |
| put off | postpone | The meeting was put off until Friday. |
| call off | cancel | The authority called off the event because of unsafe conditions. |
| bring about | cause | The reform brought about a change in service delivery. |
| point out | draw attention to | The audit pointed out a gap in the records. |
| take over | assume control/responsibility | A new officer took over the charge. |
| hand over | transfer possession/responsibility | The clerk handed over the files. |
| follow up | take further action after an earlier step | Please follow up on the pending application. |
| work out | find a solution or calculate | The two offices worked out a joint schedule. |
| find out | discover information | The inquiry found out when the notice was issued. |
| bring up | mention a subject | She brought up the delay at the meeting. |
| go through | examine carefully | The officer went through the application. |
| turn down | reject | The board turned down the incomplete proposal. |
| fill in | complete missing information | Fill in the date before submission. |
| fill out | complete a form | Applicants must fill out the form. |
| carry on | continue | The service carried on during the repair work. |
| back up | support with evidence / make a copy | The claim must be backed up by records. |
| draw up | prepare a document or plan | The committee drew up a draft schedule. |
| deal with | handle | The help desk deals with service complaints. |
| account for | explain or form a part of | The report accounts for the difference in totals. |
| make up | constitute or reconcile, depending on context | Women make up half the group. |
| run into | encounter unexpectedly | The project ran into a delay. |
| rule out | exclude as a possibility | The review ruled out a clerical error. |

Some phrasal verbs are separable: `fill out the form` / `fill the form out`; with a pronoun, the object usually goes between verb and particle: `fill it out`. Others are not separable in their ordinary meaning: `look into the complaint`, not `look the complaint into`. Learn the pattern with the expression.
### 2.2 Idioms and formal tone

| Idiom | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| at short notice | with little warning | The team assembled at short notice. |
| in the long run | over a long period | Preventive maintenance saves money in the long run. |
| on the same page | sharing the same understanding | The departments must be on the same page about the schedule. |
| a level playing field | fair conditions for participants | Clear rules help create a level playing field for bidders. |
| get the ball rolling | begin an activity | The chairperson got the ball rolling with a short briefing. |
| keep an eye on | monitor | The team kept an eye on the water level. |
| miss the point | fail to understand the main idea | A response that lists rules but ignores access misses the point. |
| make ends meet | manage basic expenses | The support helped the family make ends meet. |
| a grey area | an uncertain or unclear matter | The manual left a grey area in the procedure. |
| take something with a grain of salt | treat a claim cautiously | Take unverified online claims with a grain of salt. |
| go the extra mile | make additional effort | The staff went the extra mile to assist elderly applicants. |
| tip of the iceberg | a small visible part of a larger issue | The first complaint may be only the tip of the iceberg. |

Idioms are compact but often informal. In an official order, replace `get the ball rolling` with `begin the process`; replace `keep an eye on` with `monitor`. In a composition or essay, an idiom may be suitable if the tone remains consistent.
### 2.3 One-word substitutes

| Definition | One-word substitute | Example |
|---|---|---|
| A person who examines accounts independently | auditor | The auditor reviewed the expenditure records. |
| A person who gives evidence in court | witness | The witness described what was observed. |
| A person who applies for a post or benefit | applicant | Each applicant received a reference number. |
| A person who receives a benefit | beneficiary | The beneficiary was informed of the next step. |
| A person who makes or submits a bid | bidder | Each bidder submitted the required documents. |
| A person who studies the past through evidence | historian | The historian compared the archival records. |
| A person who writes dictionaries | lexicographer | A lexicographer records word meanings and usage. |
| A person who speaks several languages | multilingual | The multilingual officer assisted visitors. |
| A person who cannot read or write | illiterate | The programme provides learning support to adults who are illiterate. |
| A person who is new to a place or activity | novice | A novice user may need clear instructions. |
| A statement that can be proved true or false | proposition | The proposition should be tested against evidence. |
| A written account of events in order | chronicle | The chronicle recorded the sequence of events. |
| A list arranged alphabetically | glossary | The glossary explains technical terms. |
| A list of items to be discussed at a meeting | agenda | The agenda was circulated in advance. |
| A record of a meeting | minutes | The minutes were approved at the next meeting. |
| A person legally appointed to manage another’s affairs | trustee | The trustee must act within the governing rules. |
| A person who reports wrongdoing in an organization | whistle-blower | The whistle-blower shared evidence through the proper channel. |
| A person who studies human society | sociologist | The sociologist examined patterns in the survey. |
| A person who collects and studies maps | cartographer | The cartographer prepared the district map. |
| A person who moves to another country to live | immigrant | The word describes movement from the receiving country’s perspective. |

Some one-word substitutes describe a role only in a particular context. For example, a `trustee` has duties defined by the relevant trust or law. Do not infer legal powers from a vocabulary definition alone.
### 2.4 Commonly confused and misused words

| Word pair | Difference | Example |
|---|---|---|
| advice / advise | noun / verb | The adviser gave advice; she advised the team. |
| affect / effect | usually verb / usually noun | The change may affect access; the effect was measured. |
| accept / except | receive / excluding | We accept the application except for the missing annexure. |
| principal / principle | chief / rule or value | The principal officer upheld the principle of fairness. |
| stationary / stationery | not moving / writing materials | The vehicle remained stationary near the stationery store. |
| lose / loose | fail to keep / not tight | Do not lose the loose papers. |
| later / latter | after some time / second of two | We will meet later; the latter option is safer. |
| cite / site / sight | quote as authority / place / ability to see | Cite the rule; inspect the site; the sight was visible. |
| complement / compliment | complete or go well with / praise | The chart complements the report; she received a compliment. |
| ensure / insure | make certain / provide insurance | Ensure the record is complete; insure the vehicle. |
| among / between | within a group / relation involving distinct parties | Share among the teams; agreement between the two offices. |
| farther / further | physical distance / additional extent | Walk farther; provide further details. |
| imply / infer | suggest / conclude from evidence | The notice implies a deadline; the reader infers its effect. |
| its / it's | possessive / it is or it has | The office changed its hours; it's open now. |
| your / you're | possessive / you are | Your file is ready; you're welcome to collect it. |
| principle / principal | rule / main or chief | A principal reason; a guiding principle. |
### 2.5 A reliable choice method

1. Read the whole sentence, including its subject and object.
2. Identify the intended meaning and grammatical role.
3. Check whether the expression is fixed or separable.
4. Replace the candidate word with a plain synonym. If the sentence meaning changes, reconsider.
5. Check register: a conversational idiom may not fit an official notice.
6. Read the sentence once more for agreement, tense, and clarity.
## भाग 3: प्रामाणिक तथ्य, आंकड़े एवं संदर्भ

| Official syllabus statement | Study implication |
|---|---|
| General English is a 70-mark unit | Allocate revision across usage, comprehension, translation, and composition |
| Grammar & Usage is 20 marks | This chapter and Chapter 7 cover its language-use components |
| Phrasal verbs and idioms are tested in application | Practise them in sentences rather than memorizing translations only |
| One-word substitutes are listed | Learn the definition and use the substitute in a sentence |
| Words often confused or misused are listed | Compare meaning and part of speech in context |
**Official source:** [RPSC Scheme & Syllabus of Examination, dated 09-01-2026](https://rpsc.rajasthan.gov.in/Static/Syllabus/238A2E0E-B0D0-49C2-8E5E-D299A915037F.pdf)
The vocabulary examples in this chapter are practice material. The official syllabus specifies the skill areas, not a guaranteed list of expressions or fixed question allocation.
## भाग 4: स्पष्टता और तुलना: जानिए सूक्ष्म अंतर

| Similar forms | Distinction | Quick check |
|---|---|---|
| `look into` / `look at` | investigate / direct one’s gaze or attention | look into a complaint; look at a chart |
| `put off` / `call off` | postpone / cancel | put off until Friday; call off the event |
| `bring about` / `bring up` | cause / mention or raise a subject | bring about reform; bring up an issue |
| `follow up` / `follow through` | take a next step / complete a commitment | follow up on a case; follow through on a promise |
| `advice` / `advise` | noun / verb | some advice; advise a colleague |
| `affect` / `effect` | usually action / result | affect the service; measure the effect |
| `imply` / `infer` | speaker or text suggests / reader concludes | notice implies; reader infers |
| `ensure` / `insure` | make certain / arrange insurance | ensure safety; insure a vehicle |
| `stationary` / `stationery` | still / writing supplies | stationary bus; stationery cupboard |
| `its` / `it's` | possessive / contraction | its policy; it's ready |

An expression can be grammatically correct but stylistically unsuitable. A formal report may say `The committee investigated the complaint`, while a conversational passage may say `The committee looked into the complaint`. Match the register to the task.
## भाग 5: उच्च-प्रतिफल बहुविकल्पीय प्रश्न (विस्तृत व्याख्या सहित)
**Question 1:** Choose the correct phrasal verb: `The committee will ___ the complaint.`

A. look into  
B. look after to  
C. look over to (meaning investigate)  
D. look up with
**Answer: A.** `Look into` means investigate in this sentence.
**Question 2:** Choose the correct phrasal verb: `The authority ___ the event because the venue was unsafe.`

A. called off  
B. brought up  
C. looked into  
D. carried out
**Answer: A.** `Call off` means cancel.
**Question 3:** `Carry out an inspection` means:

A. perform an inspection  
B. cancel an inspection  
C. postpone an inspection  
D. forget an inspection
**Answer: A.** `Carry out` means perform or conduct.
**Question 4:** Choose the correct form: `Please ___ the missing date.`

A. fill in  
B. fill over  
C. fill through  
D. fill upon
**Answer: A.** `Fill in` means supply missing information.
**Question 5:** Choose the correct pronoun position: `Please fill ___ before submission.`

A. out it  
B. it out  
C. out with it  
D. it through
**Answer: B.** With this separable phrasal verb, the pronoun normally comes between `fill` and `out`.
**Question 6:** `The audit pointed out a gap` means the audit:

A. drew attention to a gap  
B. concealed a gap  
C. filled a gap physically  
D. cancelled the audit
**Answer: A.** `Point out` means identify or draw attention to something.
**Question 7:** Choose the best phrase: `The departments need to be ___ about the schedule.`

A. on the same page  
B. under the weather  
C. out of hand  
D. in hot water
**Answer: A.** `On the same page` means sharing the same understanding.
**Question 8:** `At short notice` means:

A. with little warning  
B. after a long delay  
C. in written form only  
D. without permission
**Answer: A.** The idiom describes something arranged or done with little advance warning.
**Question 9:** Choose the correct pair: `The change may ___ access; its ___ will be reviewed.`

A. effect / affect  
B. affect / effect  
C. advice / advise  
D. ensure / insure
**Answer: B.** `Affect` is commonly a verb meaning influence; `effect` is commonly a noun meaning result.
**Question 10:** Choose the correct word: `The officer ___ the team to retain the original file.`

A. advice  
B. advised  
C. advising (without an auxiliary)  
D. advices
**Answer: B.** `Advised` is the past-tense verb; `advice` is a noun.
**Question 11:** Choose the correct word: `The ___ of the scheme is fairness.`

A. principal  
B. principle  
C. principally  
D. principled
**Answer: B.** `Principle` means a rule or guiding value.
**Question 12:** Choose the correct word: `The ___ officer signed the note.`

A. principle  
B. principal  
C. principled  
D. principally
**Answer: B.** `Principal` can mean chief or main.
**Question 13:** Choose the correct sentence.

A. The bus remained stationary near the stationery shop.  
B. The bus remained stationery near the stationary shop.  
C. The bus remained stationary near the stationary shop (meaning writing materials).  
D. The bus remained stationery near the stationery shop.
**Answer: A.** `Stationary` means not moving; `stationery` means writing materials.
**Question 14:** Choose the correct word: `Do not ___ the receipt; the loose papers can be replaced.`

A. loose  
B. lose  
C. loss  
D. losing
**Answer: B.** `Lose` means fail to keep; `loose` means not tight.
**Question 15:** Choose the correct word: `The ___ option is less costly.`

A. later  
B. latter  
C. latest  
D. lateness
**Answer: B.** `Latter` means the second of two options.
**Question 16:** Choose the correct words: `Please ___ the relevant rule and visit the project ___.`

A. site / cite  
B. cite / site  
C. sight / cite  
D. site / sight
**Answer: B.** `Cite` means refer to a source; `site` is a place.
**Question 17:** Choose the correct word: `The chart will ___ the written report.`

A. compliment  
B. complement  
C. compliments  
D. complimentary
**Answer: B.** `Complement` means complete or go well with; `compliment` means praise.
**Question 18:** Choose the correct word: `Please ___ that every page is signed.`

A. insure  
B. ensure  
C. assure of  
D. insurance
**Answer: B.** `Ensure` means make certain.
**Question 19:** Choose the correct word: `The notice ___ a deadline, and readers may ___ that late applications will be rejected.`

A. infers / implies  
B. implies / infer  
C. implies / imply  
D. infers / infer
**Answer: B.** A text implies or suggests; a reader infers or concludes.
**Question 20:** A person who examines accounts independently is an:

A. auditor  
B. applicant  
C. lexicographer  
D. cartographer
**Answer: A.** An auditor examines accounts or related records.
**Question 21:** A person who writes dictionaries is a:

A. historian  
B. lexicographer  
C. witness  
D. beneficiary
**Answer: B.** A lexicographer compiles or writes dictionaries.
**Question 22:** A written record of a meeting is called the:

A. agenda  
B. minutes  
C. glossary  
D. chronicle only for every meeting record
**Answer: B.** Meeting minutes record discussion or decisions; an agenda lists items for discussion.
**Question 23:** A list of technical terms with brief meanings is a:

A. glossary  
B. itinerary  
C. obituary  
D. inventory only of vocabulary
**Answer: A.** A glossary explains terms used in a subject or document.
**Question 24:** A person who reports wrongdoing within an organization is commonly called a:

A. whistle-blower  
B. beneficiary  
C. novice  
D. bidder
**Answer: A.** The term describes a person who reports suspected wrongdoing through an appropriate channel.
**Question 25:** Choose the correct expression: `The board ___ the incomplete proposal.`

A. turned down  
B. turned into  
C. turned up with  
D. turned across
**Answer: A.** `Turn down` means reject.
**Question 26:** Choose the correct phrasal verb: `The team ___ a joint schedule.`

A. worked out  
B. put out  
C. ruled out  
D. took down
**Answer: A.** `Work out` can mean devise or find a solution.
**Question 27:** `Put off the meeting` means:

A. postpone it  
B. cancel it permanently in every case  
C. begin it  
D. record it
**Answer: A.** `Put off` means postpone; `call off` means cancel.
**Question 28:** Choose the correct phrasal verb: `Please ___ on the unresolved cases next week.`

A. follow up  
B. call off  
C. turn down  
D. bring about
**Answer: A.** `Follow up on` means take further action regarding an earlier matter.
**Question 29:** `The project ran into a delay` means it:

A. encountered a delay  
B. caused a delay to run  
C. ended the delay  
D. planned a delay
**Answer: A.** `Run into` means encounter unexpectedly in this context.
**Question 30:** Choose the correct phrase: `The review ___ a clerical error as the cause.`

A. ruled out  
B. drew up  
C. brought up  
D. set up
**Answer: A.** `Rule out` means exclude as a possibility.
**Question 31:** `Get the ball rolling` means:

A. begin an activity  
B. stop a meeting  
C. avoid a task  
D. record a decision
**Answer: A.** The idiom means start a process or activity.
**Question 32:** `In the long run` means:

A. over a long period  
B. immediately  
C. in writing  
D. by accident
**Answer: A.** It refers to a longer-term period or eventual effect.
**Question 33:** `A level playing field` refers to:

A. fair conditions for participants  
B. a sports ground only  
C. a long report  
D. an uncertain rule
**Answer: A.** The idiom means a fair situation with comparable conditions.
**Question 34:** Choose the best one-word substitute: `A person who receives a benefit.`

A. beneficiary  
B. bidder  
C. auditor  
D. witness
**Answer: A.** A beneficiary receives a benefit under a scheme or arrangement.
**Question 35:** Choose the best one-word substitute: `A person who makes a bid.`

A. bidder  
B. historian  
C. trustee  
D. novice
**Answer: A.** A bidder submits a bid or tender offer.
**Question 36:** Choose the best one-word substitute: `A person who studies maps and prepares them.`

A. cartographer  
B. lexicographer  
C. sociologist  
D. auditor
**Answer: A.** A cartographer makes or studies maps.
**Question 37:** Choose the correct word: `The office changed ___ working hours.`

A. it's  
B. its  
C. its'  
D. it is
**Answer: B.** `Its` is possessive. `It's` means `it is` or `it has`.
**Question 38:** Choose the correct word: `___ welcome to collect the file.`

A. Your  
B. You're  
C. Yours  
D. Youre
**Answer: B.** `You're` is the contraction of `you are`.
**Question 39:** Choose the correct word: `The applicant submitted the form ___ the annexure.`

A. accept  
B. except  
C. expectation  
D. acceptance
**Answer: B.** `Except` means excluding; `accept` means receive or agree to.
**Question 40:** `Take the claim with a grain of salt` means:

A. treat it cautiously  
B. accept it as proven  
C. copy it exactly  
D. reject every related claim
**Answer: A.** The idiom advises caution rather than automatic acceptance.
**Question 41:** Choose the correct phrase: `The chart ___ the report by showing the trend visually.`

A. complements  
B. compliments  
C. complement's  
D. complimentary
**Answer: A.** The chart completes or usefully accompanies the report.
**Question 42:** In a sentence, `among the departments` ordinarily indicates:

A. a relation within a group  
B. a relation only between exactly two parties  
C. movement into a room  
D. a period of time
**Answer: A.** `Among` commonly refers to members of a group; context still matters.
**Question 43:** Which expression is more suitable in a formal report?

A. investigate the complaint  
B. look into the complaint  
C. get the ball rolling on the complaint  
D. keep an eye on the complaint
**Answer: A.** `Investigate` is direct and formal; the others are more conversational or less precise.
**Question 44:** Which expression means prepare a draft plan?

A. draw up  
B. turn down  
C. call off  
D. run into
**Answer: A.** `Draw up` means prepare a document or plan.
**Question 45:** What is the best way to answer a vocabulary question?

A. Match the word to the sentence meaning and grammatical role  
B. Choose the longest word  
C. Use the first translation remembered  
D. Ignore the surrounding words
**Answer: A.** Meaning and grammatical role in context determine the best choice.
## भाग 6: क्विक रिवीजन: स्मरणीय बिंदु एवं संदर्भ
### 6.1 फटाफट रिवीजन: 60 परीक्षा-उपयोगी तथ्य

1. RPSC 2026 lists phrasal verbs and idioms in application.
2. The syllabus also lists one-word substitutes.
3. Often-confused or misused words are an explicit usage area.
4. A phrasal verb combines a verb with a particle or preposition.
5. Learn a phrasal verb with its sentence meaning.
6. `Carry out` means perform in the inspection example.
7. `Look into` means investigate.
8. `Set up` means establish in the help-desk example.
9. `Put off` means postpone.
10. `Call off` means cancel.
11. `Bring about` means cause.
12. `Point out` means draw attention to.
13. `Take over` can mean assume responsibility.
14. `Hand over` can mean transfer possession or responsibility.
15. `Follow up on` means take a later step on a matter.
16. `Work out` can mean find or devise a solution.
17. `Find out` means discover information.
18. `Bring up` can mean mention a subject.
19. `Go through` can mean examine carefully.
20. `Turn down` means reject.
21. `Fill in` can mean supply missing information.
22. `Fill out` can mean complete a form.
23. A pronoun generally sits between verb and particle in separable phrasal verbs.
24. `Look into` is not normally separable in its investigate sense.
25. `Rule out` means exclude as a possibility.
26. `Draw up` means prepare a document or plan.
27. `Run into` can mean encounter a difficulty.
28. `Account for` can mean explain or constitute a share.
29. `At short notice` means with little warning.
30. `In the long run` means over a longer period.
31. `On the same page` means sharing an understanding.
32. `A level playing field` means fair conditions.
33. `Get the ball rolling` means begin.
34. `Keep an eye on` means monitor.
35. `Miss the point` means fail to understand the main idea.
36. `Make ends meet` means manage essential expenses.
37. `A grey area` is uncertain or unclear.
38. `Take with a grain of salt` means treat cautiously.
39. `Go the extra mile` means make additional effort.
40. `Tip of the iceberg` means a small visible part of a larger issue.
41. `Advice` is a noun; `advise` is a verb.
42. `Affect` is commonly a verb; `effect` is commonly a noun.
43. `Accept` means receive; `except` means excluding.
44. `Principal` means chief; `principle` means rule or value.
45. `Stationary` means still; `stationery` means writing materials.
46. `Lose` means fail to keep; `loose` means not tight.
47. `Later` means after some time; `latter` means the second of two.
48. `Cite` means refer to; `site` means place; `sight` means vision or something seen.
49. `Complement` completes; `compliment` praises.
50. `Ensure` means make certain; `insure` concerns insurance.
51. A text implies; a reader infers.
52. `Its` is possessive; `it's` means `it is` or `it has`.
53. `Your` is possessive; `you're` means `you are`.
54. `Fewer` is standard with countable plural nouns.
55. `Less` is standard with uncountable amounts.
56. A glossary lists and explains subject terms.
57. An agenda lists items for a meeting.
58. Minutes record a meeting.
59. Register an idiom's tone before using it in a formal document.
60. Choose vocabulary by meaning, grammar, collocation, and register.

chapters.title: अध्याय 9: Reading Comprehension & English Précis: Read, Infer, Condense

content.value: ## भाग 1: अध्याय प्रवेश: परीक्षा दृष्टिकोण एवं विगत प्रश्न

The RPSC Paper IV syllabus dated 9 January 2026 places comprehension and précis in the 30-mark General English section. It specifies an unseen passage of approximately 300 words, five questions based on the passage, and a précis of approximately 100 words from the same passage. Follow the actual question paper if its directions set a different count or limit.

Comprehension checks what the passage says and implies. A précis tests whether the candidate can preserve the main argument while reducing detail. The safest sequence is: read for the whole point, mark the paragraph roles, answer from evidence, then write a separate concise summary.
## भाग 2: संकल्पना विस्तार: Comprehension and Précis Method
### 2.1 A two-pass reading routine

**First pass — map the passage.** Read without stopping to translate every word. Identify the topic, the author's main claim, the paragraph sequence, and the conclusion. In the margin, use short labels such as `problem`, `cause`, `evidence`, `proposal`, `limit`.

**Second pass — locate evidence.** For each question, underline the sentence or phrase that supports the answer. Distinguish explicit facts from inference. If a question asks `why`, use a stated reason; if it asks `what can be inferred`, combine clues without adding outside assumptions.

**Answer in your own words.** Keep the answer direct. Use a short quotation only when the question asks for a phrase or the passage's exact wording is uniquely important. Do not import facts from memory unless the question explicitly asks for outside knowledge.
### 2.2 Question types and how to answer

| Question type | Method | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Main idea/title | State the passage's central point | Choosing a minor example |
| Direct detail | Return to the relevant sentence | Answering from memory alone |
| Vocabulary in context | Replace the word with a synonym and reread | Using the first dictionary meaning automatically |
| Inference | Join two or more textual clues | Treating a guess as a stated fact |
| Purpose/tone | Ask what the author is trying to do | Calling every passage persuasive |
| Cause/effect | Track connectors and sequence | Reversing cause and outcome |
| Reference | Identify the noun a pronoun points to | Selecting the nearest noun if meaning conflicts |
| True/false | Compare every part of the statement to the text | Marking a partly false compound statement true |
### 2.3 Précis of the same passage

The précis uses the same passage as the comprehension questions. It is not a second opinion or a collection of answers. Keep the main argument, necessary supporting reason, and conclusion; remove examples, repeated explanations, and minor details. The official syllabus gives an approximate 100-word target. Write a coherent paragraph in your own words and count it after editing.
### 2.4 Fully worked passage
**Practice passage — approximately 300 words; original study material**

Public service centres are often judged by the number of applications they process, but speed alone does not show whether a service is accessible. A citizen may travel a long distance, wait for hours, and still leave without knowing which document is missing. A centre that records only the number of completed applications can overlook these failed visits. Service quality therefore needs measures that reflect both output and the experience of users.

One practical improvement is to explain requirements before a person makes the journey. A notice should use plain language, list essential documents, identify any fee, and state where assistance is available. The information must be updated when rules change. A notice that is technically complete but difficult to read is not useful to many citizens. Offices can also provide a help desk or a telephone contact for people who cannot easily use a website.

Digital services can reduce travel and waiting, but they do not solve every access problem. Some applicants may lack a reliable connection, a suitable device, or confidence using an online form. A digital application should therefore have a clear status tracker and a route for correcting mistakes. Where a service is offered online, an assisted offline option may still be needed. The aim is not to preserve every old process, but to ensure that a person is not excluded merely because the preferred channel is inaccessible.

Finally, offices should review complaints and incomplete applications as evidence about the service itself. If many people repeatedly miss the same requirement, the response should not be to blame applicants automatically. The office should check whether its instructions are clear and whether staff give consistent guidance. A small feedback loop—recording the problem, correcting the information, and checking whether repeat errors decline—can improve service without a costly redesign. Accessible administration combines timely processing with understandable information, human assistance, and regular learning from users.
**Comprehension questions and model answers**

1. Why does the passage say processing speed alone is insufficient?  
   **Answer:** It does not show whether citizens can use the service successfully or understand what is required.
2. Name two details that a useful notice should provide.  
   **Answer:** It should list essential documents and state any fee; it should also explain where assistance is available.
3. Why are digital services not a complete solution?  
   **Answer:** Some applicants may lack reliable internet, an appropriate device, or confidence with online forms.
4. What should an office do when many applicants make the same error?  
   **Answer:** Review whether the instructions are unclear or staff guidance is inconsistent, then correct the information and track the result.
5. What is the passage's central recommendation?  
   **Answer:** Assess services through both timely processing and user access, and use feedback to improve instructions and assistance.
**Précis — 100 words**
**Title: Measuring Accessible Public Services**

Application counts alone cannot show whether citizens can use a service. Offices should publish clear, current instructions and provide help before travel or submission. Digital channels can reduce waiting, but people without reliable access or digital confidence may still need assisted alternatives. Services should include a way to track applications and correct errors. Repeated incomplete applications and complaints can reveal unclear instructions or inconsistent staff guidance. Offices should record these problems, revise information, and check whether errors decline. Accessible administration therefore combines timely processing with understandable requirements, human assistance, and regular learning from users.
### 2.5 Précis quality checklist

- Does it express the passage's central claim?
- Are the supporting points in a logical order?
- Have examples and repeated detail been removed?
- Is every claim supported by the source passage?
- Are the words your own, with no change in meaning?
- Is the paragraph near the requested word limit?
- Is the title accurate and concise if a title is requested?
## भाग 3: प्रामाणिक तथ्य, आंकड़े एवं संदर्भ

| Official syllabus detail | Exam practice |
|---|---|
| General English: 70 marks | Prepare comprehension alongside other English units |
| Comprehension, Translation & Precis: 30 marks | This is the combined unit, not a promise that each skill receives an equal share |
| Unseen passage: approximately 300 words | Practise reading without translating each word |
| Five questions based on the passage | Answer directly from the text and its implications |
| Précis of the same passage: approximately 100 words | Condense the same text, not only the five answers |
**Official source:** [RPSC Scheme & Syllabus of Examination, dated 09-01-2026](https://rpsc.rajasthan.gov.in/Static/Syllabus/238A2E0E-B0D0-49C2-8E5E-D299A915037F.pdf)

The worked passage and answers are original practice material, not a reproduced or attributed past paper. The syllabus states approximate lengths; use the question paper's directions for the actual response.
## भाग 4: स्पष्टता और तुलना: जानिए सूक्ष्म अंतर

| Comprehension answer | Précis |
|---|---|
| Responds to a specific question | Summarizes the whole passage |
| May include a detail or inference | Selects only central ideas |
| Several short responses are possible | Usually one coherent paragraph |
| Evidence should be locatable in the text | Every point should still be supported by the text |
| Length follows each question's demand | Here the syllabus indicates about 100 words |

| Text signal | Likely function |
|---|---|
| however, but, yet | contrast or qualification |
| because, since | reason |
| therefore, consequently | result or conclusion |
| for example, such as | illustration |
| although, despite | concession |
| first, next, finally | sequence |
| only if, unless | condition |
Signals guide interpretation, but meaning depends on the full sentence. For example, `since` can refer to time or cause; read the surrounding clause.
## भाग 5: उच्च-प्रतिफल बहुविकल्पीय प्रश्न (विस्तृत व्याख्या सहित)
Questions 1–10 refer to the worked passage in Part 2. Questions 11–45 test reading and précis skills.
**Question 1:** What does the passage identify as a limitation of counting completed applications?

A. It may miss failed visits and access barriers.  
B. It always measures user satisfaction.  
C. It records the quality of every notice.  
D. It guarantees that instructions are current.
**Answer: A.** The first paragraph says completed counts can overlook citizens who leave without completing an application.
**Question 2:** Which item is not explicitly listed as useful notice information?

A. Essential documents  
B. Any fee  
C. Where assistance is available  
D. The applicant's income history
**Answer: D.** The passage lists the first three, not income history.
**Question 3:** Why may some people need an assisted offline option?

A. They may lack reliable internet, a suitable device, or confidence online.  
B. Digital services always increase travel.  
C. Websites cannot show application status.  
D. Paper forms are always faster.
**Answer: A.** These access barriers are stated in the third paragraph.
**Question 4:** What should an office infer when many applicants miss the same requirement?

A. The instructions or staff guidance may need review.  
B. Every applicant acted dishonestly.  
C. The service should be cancelled.  
D. More documents should automatically be required.
**Answer: A.** The passage recommends checking the clarity of instructions and consistency of guidance.
**Question 5:** The phrase `feedback loop` in the passage refers to:

A. recording a problem, making a correction, and checking the result  
B. repeating the same error indefinitely  
C. replacing every service with a website  
D. collecting comments without acting
**Answer: A.** The final paragraph defines the cycle in these terms.
**Question 6:** What is the central point of the passage?

A. Accessible services require timely processing, clear information, assistance, and learning from users.  
B. Online applications should replace all public counters.  
C. Application counts are useless.  
D. Every complaint proves staff misconduct.
**Answer: A.** This combines the passage's main recommendation without overgeneralizing.
**Question 7:** Which statement is supported by the passage?

A. A technically complete notice can still be hard to use.  
B. A help desk is unnecessary when a website exists.  
C. Offices should blame applicants for repeated errors.  
D. Digital applications cannot contain mistakes.
**Answer: A.** The passage directly distinguishes technical completeness from readability.
**Question 8:** In the final paragraph, `the response should not be to blame applicants automatically` means:

A. Examine the service design before assigning blame.  
B. Applicants are never responsible for any error.  
C. Complaints should be ignored.  
D. Staff must accept every application.
**Answer: A.** The author calls for checking instructions and staff guidance; the statement does not say applicants can never err.
**Question 9:** Which title best fits the passage?

A. Making Public Services Easier to Use  
B. Why All Paper Forms Must End  
C. The History of Application Registers  
D. Counting Citizens in Every Office
**Answer: A.** It captures the central concern of access and service improvement.
**Question 10:** The passage's tone is best described as:

A. practical and advisory  
B. sarcastic  
C. fictional and dramatic  
D. hostile toward applicants
**Answer: A.** It explains service problems and proposes practical improvements.
**Question 11:** What should a reader do before answering a detail question?

A. Locate the relevant passage evidence.  
B. Use unrelated background knowledge.  
C. Guess from the title alone.  
D. Write a personal opinion.
**Answer: A.** Detail answers should be grounded in the text.
**Question 12:** An inference is:

A. a conclusion supported by textual clues  
B. any outside fact the reader remembers  
C. a copied sentence without context  
D. a heading
**Answer: A.** Inference connects clues without exceeding the evidence.
**Question 13:** If a question asks for the passage's main idea, choose:

A. the central claim covering the whole text  
B. the most unusual example  
C. the last noun  
D. a minor date
**Answer: A.** A main-idea answer should represent the whole passage.
**Question 14:** In précis writing, which material is usually removed first?

A. repeated examples and minor detail  
B. the central claim  
C. the conclusion  
D. the necessary cause
**Answer: A.** Remove secondary material while preserving the reasoning.
**Question 15:** What is the best way to handle an unknown word in a passage?

A. Use surrounding clues and the sentence's role.  
B. Stop reading the entire passage.  
C. Choose the first meaning recalled.  
D. Replace it with a guessed fact.
**Answer: A.** Context often narrows a word's meaning.
**Question 16:** The word `however` most often signals:

A. contrast or qualification  
B. a list of examples  
C. a date  
D. a definition only
**Answer: A.** It commonly introduces a contrasting or qualifying point.
**Question 17:** The connector `therefore` most often signals:

A. a result or conclusion  
B. a concession  
C. a person  
D. a quotation
**Answer: A.** It introduces an inference or result.
**Question 18:** The phrase `for example` normally introduces:

A. an illustration  
B. the main conclusion  
C. an opposing claim  
D. a time marker
**Answer: A.** It signals an example that supports or clarifies a point.
**Question 19:** A précis should be written:

A. in your own words while preserving the source meaning  
B. by copying every sentence  
C. as a personal critique  
D. with additional facts from memory
**Answer: A.** A précis condenses the source without changing its meaning.
**Question 20:** The RPSC syllabus indicates an English précis of approximately:

A. 50 words  
B. 100 words  
C. 300 words  
D. 600 words
**Answer: B.** The official Paper IV syllabus gives approximately 100 words for the English précis.
**Question 21:** The unseen English passage is approximately:

A. 100 words  
B. 150 words  
C. 300 words  
D. 600 words
**Answer: C.** The syllabus specifies an unseen passage of approximately 300 words.
**Question 22:** How many passage-based questions does the syllabus indicate?

A. Two  
B. Three  
C. Five  
D. Ten
**Answer: C.** The syllabus specifies five questions based on the passage.
**Question 23:** The précis should be based on:

A. the same passage used for comprehension  
B. a different passage from memory  
C. the candidate's essay topic  
D. an unrelated news article
**Answer: A.** The syllabus states that the précis is from the same passage.
**Question 24:** What is a reliable way to determine a pronoun's reference?

A. Check which noun fits the meaning of the sentence.  
B. Always select the nearest noun.  
C. Select the longest noun.  
D. Ignore the previous sentence.
**Answer: A.** Proximity helps, but meaning and grammar determine the referent.
**Question 25:** A two-part statement is true only when:

A. both parts are supported  
B. one part is supported  
C. the first part sounds plausible  
D. the statement contains a number
**Answer: A.** A compound claim fails if either part contradicts the passage.
**Question 26:** If a question asks what the author recommends, the answer should focus on:

A. proposed action or approach  
B. the reader's preferred solution  
C. every example  
D. the passage title only
**Answer: A.** Recommendation questions ask for the author's proposed course.
**Question 27:** Which précis is stronger?

A. One that keeps the claim and necessary supporting relationships  
B. One that keeps the longest sentence  
C. One that lists every example  
D. One that changes the conclusion
**Answer: A.** The reasoning, not sentence length, determines what to retain.
**Question 28:** Why should outside knowledge usually be excluded from a comprehension answer?

A. The question asks what the passage states or implies.  
B. Outside knowledge is always wrong.  
C. It increases the word count.  
D. It changes the font.
**Answer: A.** Text-based questions are evaluated against the passage.
**Question 29:** What should a candidate do if two options seem similar?

A. Compare each option against the exact evidence and wording.  
B. Select the longer one.  
C. Select the option with an unfamiliar word.  
D. Ignore the passage.
**Answer: A.** Close comparison helps identify exaggeration or a subtle contradiction.
**Question 30:** The phrase `although` most often introduces:

A. a concession  
B. a list  
C. a result  
D. a title
**Answer: A.** `Although` signals a point conceded before a contrasting main clause.
**Question 31:** In précis editing, repeated ideas should generally be:

A. combined once  
B. repeated verbatim  
C. expanded with new examples  
D. moved into the title
**Answer: A.** Combining repetition saves words and improves focus.
**Question 32:** What should a précis title do?

A. Identify the central subject accurately  
B. Introduce a new claim  
C. Quote an unverified author  
D. Replace the summary
**Answer: A.** A title should reflect, not alter, the passage's main point.
**Question 33:** Which answer best demonstrates an inference?

A. A cautious conclusion drawn from multiple textual clues  
B. A statement copied from an unrelated source  
C. A guess with no evidence  
D. A personal preference
**Answer: A.** Inference relies on clues rather than unsupported speculation.
**Question 34:** If a passage gives a problem and then a solution, what does `therefore` likely connect?

A. evidence or reasons to a conclusion  
B. two unrelated names  
C. a title to a date  
D. a quote to a page number
**Answer: A.** The connector commonly marks a logical consequence.
**Question 35:** How can a reader avoid confusing a supporting example with the main idea?

A. Ask whether it represents the whole passage or only illustrates one point.  
B. Choose the most concrete sentence automatically.  
C. Ignore the opening paragraph.  
D. Count the nouns.
**Answer: A.** Examples support an idea but rarely state the whole argument.
**Question 36:** What does a tone question ask?

A. The author's attitude or manner of presentation  
B. The number of paragraphs  
C. The author's personal identity  
D. The meaning of every noun
**Answer: A.** Tone concerns how the author presents the subject.
**Question 37:** Which is the best approach to a vocabulary-in-context question?

A. Substitute a likely meaning and reread the sentence.  
B. Memorize an unrelated synonym list.  
C. Ignore the surrounding clause.  
D. Choose the rarest option.
**Answer: A.** Substitution tests whether the meaning fits the passage.
**Question 38:** A précis that adds a recommendation absent from the source:

A. changes the source and is inaccurate  
B. is always stronger  
C. is a translation  
D. is required by the syllabus
**Answer: A.** A précis should not invent content.
**Question 39:** A very short précis may be weak because it:

A. omits essential reasoning  
B. always uses too many examples  
C. automatically changes the font  
D. becomes a title
**Answer: A.** Excessive compression can remove the main supporting relationships.
**Question 40:** A very long précis may be weak because it:

A. retains too much detail and misses the reduction task  
B. preserves the central idea  
C. uses a title  
D. is based on the correct passage
**Answer: A.** It may fail to condense the text to the requested scale.
**Question 41:** What should a candidate do when the passage's conclusion qualifies an earlier claim?

A. Preserve the qualification in the answer or précis.  
B. Omit it automatically.  
C. Reverse the claim.  
D. Replace it with an absolute statement.
**Answer: A.** Qualifications affect the author's actual meaning.
**Question 42:** What does `unless` usually introduce?

A. a condition  
B. a result already achieved  
C. a person  
D. an example only
**Answer: A.** `Unless` means except if and sets a condition.
**Question 43:** What is the most useful note-taking format during a short passage?

A. Brief labels for paragraph roles and key links  
B. A full translation of every line  
C. A list of unrelated words  
D. The final answer before reading
**Answer: A.** Short structural notes preserve time and argument flow.
**Question 44:** Before submitting comprehension answers, check that:

A. each answer addresses the question and has textual support  
B. each answer contains an outside fact  
C. all answers have the same wording  
D. every answer is a full paragraph
**Answer: A.** Relevance and evidence matter more than uniform length.
**Question 45:** What is the final check for a précis?

A. Meaning, logical order, own wording, and word limit  
B. Number of examples copied  
C. Whether outside facts were added  
D. Whether the title is longer than the précis
**Answer: A.** These checks protect accuracy and concision.
## भाग 6: क्विक रिवीजन: स्मरणीय बिंदु एवं संदर्भ
### 6.1 फटाफट रिवीजन: 60 परीक्षा-उपयोगी तथ्य

1. RPSC 2026 gives 30 marks to English comprehension, translation, and précis together.
2. The unseen English passage is approximately 300 words.
3. The syllabus indicates five questions based on the passage.

chapters.title: अध्याय 10: Translation Techniques: Hindi and English with Meaning Intact

content.value: ## भाग 1: अध्याय प्रवेश: परीक्षा दृष्टिकोण एवं विगत प्रश्न

The 2026 RPSC Paper IV syllabus tests translation in both language units, with different directions. In General Hindi, candidates translate an English passage into Hindi, approximately 50 words. In General English, the syllabus lists translation of five sentences from Hindi into English. Follow the actual paper's word limit and format if they differ.

Good translation carries the meaning, relationships, tone, and relevant detail of the source into natural target-language sentences. It is neither word-for-word substitution nor an opportunity to add explanation. This chapter gives a method for both directions and original practice examples.
## भाग 2: संकल्पना विस्तार: Meaning-First Translation
### 2.1 A six-step method

1. **Read the full source.** Identify who acts, what happens, to whom, when, and why.
2. **Mark the sentence structure.** Find the main verb, subject, object, condition, and connectors.
3. **Identify terms that need a stable equivalent.** Use a known official term for an office, document, law, or scheme; do not invent a new name.
4. **Draft in natural target-language order.** Hindi and English do not always place words in the same order.
5. **Check tense, number, gender, pronouns, and register.** Preserve a formal tone where the source is official.
6. **Compare against the source.** Ensure that no fact has been added, removed, or reversed.
### 2.2 Hindi to English: sentence patterns

| Hindi pattern | Natural English choice | Watch for |
|---|---|---|
| अधिकारी ने सूचना जारी की। | The officer issued the notice. | Past action; active voice |
| आवेदन पर विचार किया जाएगा। | The application will be considered. | Passive voice is suitable when actor is unspecified |
| कृपया अभिलेख संलग्न करें। | Please attach the record. | Polite imperative |
| यदि दस्तावेज अधूरे हैं, तो आवेदन लौटाया जा सकता है। | If the documents are incomplete, the application may be returned. | Preserve condition and possibility |
| बैठक के बाद प्रतिवेदन प्रस्तुत किया गया। | The report was submitted after the meeting. | Do not invent the submitter |

**Hindi connectors:** `क्योंकि` can be `because`; `इसलिए` can be `therefore/so`; `हालांकि` can be `although/however` depending on clause structure; `यदि` is usually `if`. Translate the relation, not a fixed word list.
### 2.3 English to Hindi: paragraph method

For the Hindi-unit passage, first identify the paragraph's main point. Then translate each necessary idea in a clear Hindi sentence. Keep the source facts and sequence; do not shorten by dropping an essential idea. If a technical English term has a familiar administrative Hindi equivalent, use it consistently. If the proper name should remain in English or a standard transliteration, do not translate it literally.
**Source passage — approximately 50 words; original practice**

Before a public meeting, the district office should publish the agenda, venue, and time in accessible formats. Residents who cannot attend should have another way to submit comments. The chair should record decisions and assign follow-up responsibility. Clear records help participants understand what was agreed and when the next review will take place.
**Model Hindi translation**

सार्वजनिक बैठक से पहले जिला कार्यालय को कार्यसूची, स्थान और समय सुलभ प्रारूपों में प्रकाशित करना चाहिए। जो निवासी उपस्थित नहीं हो सकते, उनके लिए सुझाव देने का दूसरा माध्यम होना चाहिए। अध्यक्ष को निर्णय दर्ज करके आगे की कार्रवाई की जिम्मेदारी तय करनी चाहिए। स्पष्ट अभिलेख प्रतिभागियों को स्वीकृत बातों और अगली समीक्षा का समय समझने में मदद करते हैं।
This translation preserves the source's four ideas: advance information, an alternative participation channel, recorded decisions with assigned responsibility, and the value of clear records.
### 2.4 Ten model Hindi-to-English translations

1. **Hindi:** अधिकारी ने अभिलेखों की जांच की।  
   **English:** The officer examined the records.
2. **Hindi:** कृपया आवेदन के साथ पहचान-पत्र की प्रति संलग्न करें।  
   **English:** Please attach a copy of the identity document to the application.
3. **Hindi:** बैठक कल प्रातः दस बजे आयोजित होगी।  
   **English:** The meeting will be held tomorrow at 10 a.m.
4. **Hindi:** समिति ने शिकायत की जांच करने का निर्णय लिया।  
   **English:** The committee decided to investigate the complaint.
5. **Hindi:** यदि कोई दस्तावेज लंबित हो, तो आवेदक को सूचित करें।  
   **English:** If any document is outstanding, inform the applicant.
6. **Hindi:** प्रतिवेदन सक्षम प्राधिकारी को भेज दिया गया है।  
   **English:** The report has been sent to the competent authority.
7. **Hindi:** सभी विभागों से समय पर सूचना देने का अनुरोध है।  
   **English:** All departments are requested to provide the information on time.
8. **Hindi:** योजना का लाभ पात्र परिवारों तक पहुंचना चाहिए।  
   **English:** The scheme's benefits should reach eligible families.
9. **Hindi:** विवाद का समाधान बातचीत से किया जा सकता है।  
   **English:** The dispute can be resolved through discussion.
10. **Hindi:** कार्यालय ने नागरिकों की सुविधा के लिए नई खिड़की शुरू की।  
    **English:** The office opened a new counter for the convenience of citizens.
### 2.5 Ten model English-to-Hindi translations

1. **English:** The department reviewed the proposal.  
   **Hindi:** विभाग ने प्रस्ताव की समीक्षा की।
2. **English:** Please submit the form before Friday.  
   **Hindi:** कृपया शुक्रवार से पहले प्रपत्र जमा करें।
3. **English:** The order will take effect next month.  
   **Hindi:** आदेश अगले महीने से प्रभावी होगा।
4. **English:** The applicant may request a copy of the decision.  
   **Hindi:** आवेदक निर्णय की प्रति मांग सकता है।
5. **English:** The officer recorded the reasons for the delay.  
   **Hindi:** अधिकारी ने देरी के कारण दर्ज किए।
6. **English:** Residents can send comments through the public portal.  
   **Hindi:** निवासी जन-पोर्टल के माध्यम से सुझाव भेज सकते हैं।
7. **English:** The committee will meet again after the inspection.  
   **Hindi:** निरीक्षण के बाद समिति की फिर बैठक होगी।
8. **English:** Keep the receipt for future reference.  
   **Hindi:** भविष्य में संदर्भ के लिए रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
9. **English:** The instructions are available in both languages.  
   **Hindi:** निर्देश दोनों भाषाओं में उपलब्ध हैं।
10. **English:** No decision was taken until the evidence was reviewed.  
    **Hindi:** साक्ष्यों की समीक्षा होने तक कोई निर्णय नहीं लिया गया।
These translations are illustrative. Several natural renderings may be correct if they preserve the same meaning and register.
### 2.6 Common translation errors

| Error | Why it fails | Better approach |
|---|---|---|
| Translating each word in source order | Target sentence becomes unnatural or unclear | Rebuild the sentence in target-language order |
| Changing a possibility into certainty | Modality changes the claim | Preserve `may`, `can`, `must`, or their equivalents |
| Dropping `if`, `unless`, or `although` | Logical relationship changes | Preserve condition or contrast |
| Adding an actor absent from a passive source | Adds an unsupported fact | Keep passive or use a neutral construction |
| Rendering an official term inconsistently | Reader may think it names two things | Choose a standard equivalent and use it consistently |
| Translating a proper name literally | The official identity may be lost | Retain or transliterate the official name |
| Changing singular/plural or tense | Timeline or quantity changes | Compare each verb and noun against the source |

The original sample is not a previous examination question.
## भाग 4: स्पष्टता और तुलना: जानिए सूक्ष्म अंतर

| Translation choice | What it preserves | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Literal translation | Word order, often at the expense of meaning | Avoid when target syntax becomes unnatural |
| Meaning-based translation | Intended message and relationship | `अभिलेख संलग्न करें` → `Attach the record` |
| Transliteration | Sound/name in another script | Official scheme or place name |
| Translation of an official term | Meaning in an accepted administrative equivalent | `प्रतिवेदन` → `report` |
| Transcreation/adaptation | Recasts a message for a new audience | Not the task in a faithful exam translation |

| Source feature | Translation check |
|---|---|
| `may/can` | preserve possibility or permission |
| `must/should` | preserve obligation or recommendation |
| conditional clause | preserve the condition and outcome |
| passive construction | do not invent an actor |
| date, number, name | copy exactly and verify |
| formal request | use a courteous, appropriately formal target phrase |
| idiom | translate the intended meaning, not the literal image |
## भाग 5: उच्च-प्रतिफल बहुविकल्पीय प्रश्न (विस्तृत व्याख्या सहित)
**Question 1:** Translate correctly: `अधिकारी ने अभिलेखों की जांच की।`

A. The officer examined the records.  
B. The officer examination the records.  
C. The officer was examine records.  
D. The officer has examining the records yesterday.
**Answer: A.** It uses the correct past-tense verb and plural object.
**Question 2:** Translate correctly: `कृपया आवेदन संलग्न करें।`

A. Please attach the application.  
B. Please attached the application.  
C. Please attachment application.  
D. Please to attach application yesterday.
**Answer: A.** A polite imperative uses the base verb `attach`.
**Question 3:** Translate `यदि दस्तावेज अधूरे हैं, तो आवेदन लौटाया जा सकता है.`

A. If the documents are incomplete, the application may be returned.  
B. The documents are incomplete because the application returned.  
C. The application must never be returned.  
D. Although the documents are complete, return the application.
**Answer: A.** It preserves the condition and possibility expressed by `जा सकता है`.
**Question 4:** Translate `The order will take effect next month.`

D. आदेश के कारण महीना प्रभावी होगा।
**Answer: A.** It preserves the future time and meaning of taking effect.
**Question 5:** Which translation preserves the passive meaning without inventing an actor? `The report was submitted after the meeting.`

D. बैठक ने प्रतिवेदन प्रस्तुत किया।

**Question 6:** Translate `All departments are requested to provide the information on time.`

D. समय पर विभागों को अनुरोध सूचना है।

**Question 7:** Translate `कृपया शुक्रवार से पहले प्रपत्र जमा करें।`

A. Please submit the form before Friday.  
B. Please submitted the form after Friday.  
C. The form submits Friday before you.  
D. Please submit Friday to the form.

**Question 8:** In translation, `may be returned` should preserve:

A. possibility  
B. certainty  
C. past completion  
D. prohibition

**Question 9:** Translate `Keep the receipt for future reference.`

A. भविष्य में संदर्भ के लिए रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।

**Question 10:** Which approach is best for translating an official term?

A. Use a standard equivalent consistently.  
B. Invent a new translation in every sentence.  
C. Translate the letters one by one.  
D. Omit it automatically.
**Answer: A.** Consistent standard terminology reduces ambiguity.
**Question 11:** A source sentence contains `unless`. What must the translation preserve?

A. The condition  
B. Only the subject  
C. A new example

**Question 12:** Translate `Residents can send comments through the public portal.`

A. निवासी जन-पोर्टल के माध्यम से सुझाव भेज सकते हैं।

**Question 13:** Which is the most natural English translation of `विवाद का समाधान बातचीत से किया जा सकता है`?

**Question 14:** When the source uses a proper scheme name, the translator should usually:

A. retain or use its standard transliteration  
B. translate each part literally  
C. replace it with a different scheme  
D. omit it
**Answer: A.** Preserving the official identity is more important than a literal rendering.
**Question 15:** Translate `The applicant may request a copy of the decision.`

A. आवेदक निर्णय की प्रति मांग सकता है।

**Question 16:** What should a translator do when the source is passive and the actor is unknown?

A. Keep a passive or neutral construction.  
B. Invent the department as actor.  
C. Change the time.  
D. Delete the action.
**Answer: A.** Adding an actor would introduce unsupported information.
**Question 17:** Translate `बैठक कल प्रातः दस बजे आयोजित होगी।`

A. The meeting will be held tomorrow at 10 a.m.  
B. The meeting was held yesterday at ten.  
C. The meeting holds the morning.  
D. The meeting may have held next week.
**Answer: A.** It preserves the future, date reference, and time.
**Question 18:** A translation changes `should` to `must`. What has changed?

A. The strength of obligation  
B. The spelling only  
C. The speaker's name  
D. The number of objects
**Answer: A.** `Must` is usually stronger than `should`; preserve the source's force.
**Question 19:** Translate `The instructions are available in both languages.`

A. निर्देश दोनों भाषाओं में उपलब्ध हैं।

D. निर्देश एक भाषा में अनुपलब्ध थे।
**Answer: A.** It preserves availability and the two-language detail.
**Question 20:** What is the first step before translating a paragraph?

A. Read the whole paragraph and identify its main point.  
B. Translate the first word immediately.  
C. Replace every noun with a synonym.  
D. Count punctuation marks.
**Answer: A.** Understanding the whole paragraph prevents local word choices from distorting the meaning.
**Question 21:** Translate `समिति ने शिकायत की जांच करने का निर्णय लिया।`

A. The committee decided to investigate the complaint.  
B. The complaint decided to inspect the committee.  
C. The committee decision the complaint investigated.  
D. The committee has deciding the complaint yesterday.
**Answer: A.** It preserves the actor, decision, and infinitive action.
**Question 22:** Which translation preserves `because` as a reason?

A. सेवा बंद रही क्योंकि मरम्मत चल रही थी।  
B. सेवा बंद रही हालांकि मरम्मत चल रही थी।  
C. सेवा बंद रही यदि मरम्मत चल रही थी।  
D. सेवा बंद रही और मरम्मत चल रही थी, without a causal link.

**Question 23:** Translate `The committee will meet again after the inspection.`

A. निरीक्षण के बाद समिति की फिर बैठक होगी।  
B. समिति ने निरीक्षण से पहले बैठक की।  
C. निरीक्षण समिति की बैठक है।  
D. समिति बैठक के बाद निरीक्षण करेगी yesterday.
**Answer: A.** It preserves the future meeting and its sequence after inspection.
**Question 24:** Why is word-for-word translation risky?

A. Target-language word order and collocations may differ.  
B. Every source word is untranslatable.  
C. It always shortens the text.  
D. It removes the source meaning automatically.
**Answer: A.** Natural syntax and idiomatic combinations differ between languages.
**Question 25:** Translate `No decision was taken until the evidence was reviewed.`

A. साक्ष्यों की समीक्षा होने तक कोई निर्णय नहीं लिया गया।  
B. साक्ष्यों की समीक्षा के बाद निर्णय पहले ही लिया गया था।

D. समीक्षा ने निर्णय लिया।
**Answer: A.** It preserves the negative action and the time condition.
**Question 26:** What should happen to a number in translation?

A. Copy it accurately and verify it against the source.  
B. Round it without instruction.  
C. Omit every number.  
D. Replace it with a familiar figure.
**Answer: A.** Numbers are factual content and must remain accurate.
**Question 27:** Translate `योजना का लाभ पात्र परिवारों तक पहुंचना चाहिए।`

A. The scheme's benefits should reach eligible families.  
B. The plan families should benefit to arrive.  
C. The benefit has reached every family.  
D. Eligible families should scheme the benefit.
**Answer: A.** It preserves the recommendation, beneficiaries, and direction of benefit.
**Question 28:** When should an idiom be translated by meaning rather than literally?

A. When a literal image would be unnatural or misleading in the target language.  
B. Never  
C. Only in a title  
D. Whenever the source has a verb
**Answer: A.** Preserve the idiom's intended meaning, not an unsuitable word image.
**Question 29:** Translate `The officer recorded the reasons for the delay.`

A. अधिकारी ने देरी के कारण दर्ज किए।  
B. अधिकारी ने देरी को कारण बनाया।  
C. देरी ने अधिकारी को दर्ज किया।  
D. अधिकारी कारण से विलंब होगा।
**Answer: A.** It preserves the action and the object recorded.
**Question 30:** If the source says `the application may be returned`, translating it as `will be returned`:

A. changes possibility into certainty  
B. changes a noun into an adjective  
C. preserves the exact modality  
D. changes English into English only
**Answer: A.** `May` and `will` express different degrees of certainty.
**Question 31:** Translate `Residents who cannot attend should have another way to submit comments.`

A. जो निवासी उपस्थित नहीं हो सकते, उनके पास सुझाव देने का दूसरा माध्यम होना चाहिए।  
B. निवासी उपस्थित नहीं हुए क्योंकि सुझाव बंद हैं।  
C. जो सुझाव उपस्थित हैं, उन्हें निवासी करना चाहिए।  
D. निवासी दूसरा माध्यम थे।
**Answer: A.** It preserves the relative clause, recommendation, and alternative channel.
**Question 32:** A translation should preserve which source features?

A. Meaning, relationships, relevant detail, and tone  
B. Word order only  
C. Punctuation but not meaning  
D. The translator's opinion
**Answer: A.** Faithful translation carries content and communicative force.
**Question 33:** Translate `The office opened a new counter for the convenience of citizens.`

A. कार्यालय ने नागरिकों की सुविधा के लिए नया काउंटर शुरू किया।  
B. नागरिकों ने कार्यालय को सुविधा दी।  
C. काउंटर नागरिकों ने खोला।  
D. कार्यालय सुविधा का नया नागरिक है।
**Answer: A.** It preserves actor, action, object, and purpose.
**Question 34:** What should be done with an ambiguous source sentence?

A. Use context; do not silently invent a specific interpretation beyond it.  
B. Add a new fact.  
C. Omit the whole sentence.  
D. Change the subject.
**Answer: A.** Translation should preserve the source's level of specificity.
**Question 35:** Translate `The report has been sent to the competent authority.`

A. प्रतिवेदन सक्षम प्राधिकारी को भेज दिया गया है।  
B. प्राधिकारी ने प्रतिवेदन भेजा होगा, certainly.  
C. रिपोर्ट अधिकार के लिए है।  
D. रिपोर्ट सक्षम थी और भेजी जाएगी।
**Answer: A.** It preserves the completed action and recipient without inventing an actor.
**Question 36:** Which is the best approach to a proper name?

A. Preserve the official name or standard transliteration.  
B. Translate its syllables literally.  
C. Replace it with a synonym.  
D. Drop it from every sentence.
**Answer: A.** Official names identify specific entities.
**Question 37:** Translate `The order will be reviewed if new evidence is received.`

A. नया साक्ष्य मिलने पर आदेश की समीक्षा की जाएगी।  
B. नया साक्ष्य मिलने के बाद आदेश कभी नहीं देखा जाएगा।  
C. आदेश नया साक्ष्य प्राप्त करेगा।  
D. आदेश की समीक्षा हुई क्योंकि कोई साक्ष्य नहीं था।
**Answer: A.** It preserves the conditional review.
**Question 38:** Why should a translator proofread target-language agreement?

A. Correct meaning can still be obscured by wrong number or tense.  
B. Agreement is unrelated to translation.  
C. Every source noun is singular.  
D. Proofreading adds new content.
**Answer: A.** Target-language grammar must be correct as well as source-faithful.
**Question 39:** Which translation preserves a polite request?

A. Please submit the form before Friday.  
B. You submitted the form last Friday.  
C. Submit the form or else, when no threat exists in source.  
D. The form was Friday.
**Answer: A.** It keeps the courteous request and deadline.
**Question 40:** Translation of `सभी विभागों से सूचना मांगी गई` should not:

A. invent which officer requested it if the source does not say  
B. preserve the departments as recipients  
C. use a passive sentence  
D. preserve the past tense
**Answer: A.** Adding an actor would add information absent from the source.
**Question 41:** In an English-to-Hindi paragraph translation, the main paragraph point should be:

A. preserved along with its key supporting ideas  
B. replaced by a shorter unrelated thought  
C. omitted if one word is difficult  
D. expanded with personal advice
**Answer: A.** The translation should carry all essential ideas.
**Question 42:** Which is a useful final comparison question?

A. Did I add, omit, or reverse any important detail?  
B. Did I use the longest available word?  
C. Did I change the names to familiar ones?  
D. Did I remove all connectors?
**Answer: A.** A source-target comparison catches the most serious fidelity errors.
**Question 43:** Translate `The application was received on 12 July.`

A. आवेदन 12 जुलाई को प्राप्त हुआ।  
B. आवेदन 12 अगस्त को भेजा गया।  
C. आवेदन जुलाई तक प्राप्त होगा।  
D. 12 आवेदन जुलाई को थे।
**Answer: A.** It preserves the event, date, and passive sense.
**Question 44:** What is the best choice when more than one target-language rendering is natural?

A. Choose the clear one that preserves meaning and register.  
B. Assume only a word-for-word version can be correct.  
C. Add explanation until all ambiguity disappears.  
D. Copy a dictionary entry.
**Answer: A.** Translation is judged by fidelity and natural target-language expression.
**Question 45:** The current RPSC syllabus specifically asks English-unit translation of:

A. five sentences from Hindi to English  
B. a 600-word essay from Hindi to English  
C. five English sentences into Sanskrit  
D. a 300-word English passage into Hindi in the English unit
**Answer: A.** The five Hindi-to-English sentences belong to General English Part B.
## भाग 6: क्विक रिवीजन: स्मरणीय बिंदु एवं संदर्भ
### 6.1 फटाफट रिवीजन: 60 परीक्षा-उपयोगी तथ्य

1. RPSC 2026 tests translation in both language units, with different directions.
2. General Hindi translates an English paragraph into Hindi.
3. The Hindi-unit passage is approximately 50 words.
4. General English translates five sentences from Hindi into English.
5. Follow the actual paper's specific translation instructions.
6. Read the whole source before translating a paragraph.
7. Identify the main subject and action.
8. Mark object, time, cause, condition, and contrast.
9. Translate the relationship, not only individual words.
10. Rebuild word order naturally in the target language.
11. Preserve the source tense.
12. Preserve singular and plural meaning.
13. Preserve the source's degree of certainty.
14. `May` can indicate possibility or permission by context.
15. `Must` is stronger than `should` in ordinary use.
16. Keep conditional clauses such as `if` and `unless`.
17. Preserve contrast introduced by `although` or `however`.
18. Do not invent an actor absent from a passive source.
19. Use passive construction if it preserves the source emphasis.
20. Use active voice when the source names the actor and action.
21. Translate official terms consistently.
22. Check administrative terms against a reliable glossary.
23. Retain proper names or use a standard transliteration.
24. Do not translate official names literally by syllable.
25. Translate idioms by intended meaning where a literal image misleads.
26. Do not add a recommendation absent from the source.
27. Do not drop essential supporting detail from a paragraph.
28. Verify all dates and numbers against the source.
29. Keep a formal register for formal source material.
30. Use natural collocations in the target language.
31. English word order need not match Hindi word order.
32. Hindi word order need not match English word order.
33. A polite imperative often begins with `Please` in English.
34. `अभिलेख` can be translated as `record` in context.
35. `प्रतिवेदन` can be translated as `report` in context.
36. `सक्षम प्राधिकारी` is `competent authority` in administrative usage.
37. `संलग्न करें` often means `attach` in document instructions.
38. `प्रभावी होगा` can mean `will take effect`.
39. `जांच करना` can be `examine` or `investigate` depending on context.
40. `प्रार्थना/अनुरोध` requires a suitable polite register.
41. Do not translate a word by its first memorized meaning alone.
42. Read the source clause around a technical word.
43. Use connectors to preserve logic.
44. Check the target-language subject-verb agreement.
45. Check article and preposition use in English output.
46. Check gender, number, and postpositions in Hindi output.
47. Compare the final version with the source line by line.
48. Check for added information.
49. Check for omitted information.
50. Check that no cause and result have been reversed.
51. More than one translation may be natural and correct.
52. Clarity and fidelity matter more than literal word order.
53. Do not claim a practice example is a previous RPSC question.
54. Keep sentence translations concise.
55. Preserve the same names and actors across linked sentences.
56. Preserve dates, amounts, and reference numbers exactly.
57. Translate paragraph meaning as a connected whole.
58. Hindi paragraph translation should not become a summary.
59. Translation is distinct from précis writing.
60. Final check: meaning, grammar, register, and source fidelity.
